text:
anya: FYI seeing intermittent gRPC stream stalls from infer-gateway in us-west-2. small RPCs are fine, but streaming responses with larger frames hang ~20-40s then resume. started ~10:24 UTC. any ideas?

darren: which nodes/services? packet drops or TCP retransmits in node metrics?

anya: spread across 3 nodes (n-phi-02/03/04). logs show repeated: `rpc error: code = Unknown desc = stream broken: grpc: the client connection is closing` and on the node dmesg: 
```
[  123.456789] [UFW BLOCK] IN=eth0 OUT= MAC=.. SRC=10.240.1.5 DST=10.240.2.3 LEN=1512 TOS=0x00 PREC=0x00 TTL=63 ID=54321 DF PROTO=TCP SPT=45678 DPT=9000 WINDOW=64240 RES=0x00 SYN URGP=0
```

leo: quick check — can you `ip link` and `ip route` on both nodes? this smells like MTU/overlay mismatch. gRPC streaming sends large chunks so fragmentation matters.

anya: ran `ip link show` on the two nodes, copy below: 
```
# node n-phi-02
2: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
# node n-phi-03
2: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```

maria: yep that's a problem — one host has host-interface MTU 9000 (jumbo) while the other is 1500. overlay (vxlan) + CNI can add ~50 bytes overhead; if one side expects jumbo and the other doesn't, fragmentation/pmtu blackholes show up for large packets. :thinking:  

darren: do you see any iptables or offload-related log messages? sometimes GSO/GRO/TCP segmentation offload masks issues until packets traverse path that can't handle them. try disabling offloads as a quick test.

leo: commands to test:
```
# on both nodes
ip link show eth0
ip route get 10.240.2.3
iperf3 -c <peer> -u -b 100M
ethtool -k eth0 | sed -n '1,40p'
ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off
```

anya: ran `ethtool -k` — GSO/GRO/TCP segmentation is on for the 9000-MTU node. after disabling gso/gro/tso on the jumbo node the streaming stalls stopped immediately. :white_check_mark:  We rolled back the recent CNI MTU change that had set MTU=9000 on a subset of hosts.

maria: good catch. follow-ups: ensure CNI daemonset sets MTU consistently across AZs, add a node-lifecycle check to detect mixed MTU in the cluster, and add a preflight gating test for CNI MTU on deploys.

darren: created INFRA-1298 to track RCA + remediation (daemonset to normalize MTU, e2e to detect fragmentation blackholes, and a runbook). assigning to net eng-owner.

ops-bot: deploy bot: rolling update calc-scheduler completed at 10:22:41 UTC. (might have coincided with nodes getting new CNI config)

leo: additional mitigation: enable `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on gateway nodes to avoid PMTU blackholes until we normalize MTU; also prefer smaller max frame sizes for streaming frames (chunking) in the app if possible.

anya: reproduction steps added to ticket:
1) ensure nodes with mismatched MTU (1500 vs 9000)
2) start a long-lived gRPC streaming call that sends ~2KB frames repeatedly
3) observe stream stalls and `broken pipe` logs
4) flip offload with `ethtool -K` or align MTU on both sides and observe resolution

maria: 👍 also will add a CI check that fails if any node reports MTU != cluster-default on join.

darren: thanks everyone — logging the incident as Sev-3 since user impact was partial and mitigated. will post RCA draft in #postmortems tomorrow.

anya: TL;DR — root cause: mixed MTU + host offloads + vxlan overlay created fragmentation/PMTU blackhole for gRPC large frames; mitigation = revert CNI MTU change, disable offloads temporarily, and roll out MTU normalization daemonset. :memo:
